Her TSH and free T4 are normal.
Ultrasound shows a diffusely enlarged thyroid with a few small benign-looking nodules.
A 27-year-old woman has not had a period for six months.
She is not pregnant and has not changed weight.
She notices milky fluid from both nipples.
She takes no medicines and her thyroid tests are normal.
Her prolactin is very high.
MRI shows a 7 mm adenoma in the pituitary gland.
A 14-year-old boy is embarrassed by a tender lump under both nipples.
It started six months ago.
He is otherwise growing normally and his voice is breaking.
He takes no drugs or supplements.
There is a soft, rubbery disc of tissue 2 cm across behind each nipple; his testes are normal size.
His hormone tests are normal for his stage of puberty.
A 40-year-old man has burning pain in the upper abdomen since yesterday.
He had back pain and took ibuprofen several times a day for a week.
He also drank heavily at a wedding two days ago.
He feels sick and has vomited once, without blood.
His upper abdomen is tender, but there is no guarding.
Endoscopy shows red, inflamed stomach lining with small erosions and no ulcer.
A 31-year-old woman has pain when passing stool for three weeks.
She describes it as like passing broken glass, and it lasts for an hour afterwards.
She has been constipated since starting iron tablets.
She notices bright red blood on the toilet paper.
Gentle parting of the buttocks shows a small split in the skin.
The tear is in the posterior midline of the anal canal.
A 49-year-old man is referred because of abnormal liver tests on a routine check.
He feels well and drinks alcohol only at holidays.
He has type 2 diabetes, high cholesterol and central obesity.
His ALT is mildly raised, higher than his AST.
Viral hepatitis tests and autoimmune tests are negative.
Ultrasound shows a bright, enlarged liver from fat.
A newborn baby boy seems floppy at the first examination.
His mother is 41 years old.
He has upslanting eyes, a flat face and small ears.
There is a single crease across each palm and a wide gap between the first and second toes.
An echocardiogram shows an atrioventricular septal defect.
Chromosome analysis shows three copies of chromosome 21.
A 15-year-old girl has not started her periods.
She is the shortest girl in her class.
She has a webbed neck and a low hairline at the back.
Her chest is broad with widely spaced nipples.
Her FSH and LH are very high.
Karyotype shows 45,X.
A 30-year-old man comes with his wife because they cannot have children.
He is tall, with long legs.
He has little body hair and mild breast enlargement.
His testes are small and firm.
Semen analysis shows no sperm, and his FSH and LH are high with low testosterone.
Karyotype shows 47,XXY.
A 5-year-old boy is assessed for speech delay and learning problems.
He avoids eye contact and flaps his hands when excited.
His mother's brother has intellectual disability.
He has a long face, large ears and a prominent jaw.
His joints are very flexible.
DNA testing shows more than 200 CGG repeats in the FMR1 gene.
A baby girl is born with short arms and legs.
Her parents are both of average height.
Her head is large with a prominent forehead.
Her fingers are short and spread apart in a 'trident' shape.
X-rays show short long bones and a narrow spinal canal.
Testing finds a gain-of-function mutation in FGFR3.
A 4-year-old boy falls often and cannot keep up with other children.
He started walking late, at 18 months.
He climbs up his own legs with his hands to stand from the floor.
His calves look large and firm.
His creatine kinase is extremely high.
Genetic testing shows a deletion in the dystrophin gene.
A 9-month-old boy from a Mediterranean family is pale and feeding poorly.
He is not growing well.
His belly is swollen with a large liver and spleen.
His hemoglobin is 6 g/dL with very small red cells.
The blood film shows target cells and nucleated red cells.
Hemoglobin electrophoresis shows almost no HbA and high HbF.
A 10-year-old boy has had yellow eyes several times when he caught colds.
His father had his spleen removed as a young man.
He now has a mildly enlarged spleen.
His hemoglobin is low with a high MCHC and raised reticulocytes.
The blood film shows small round red cells without central pallor.
The EMA binding test is reduced and the direct Coombs test is negative.
A 6-year-old boy is short for his age.

X-ray shows a lytic lesion with ring-and-arc calcifications.
Biopsy shows malignant cartilage cells.
A 25-year-old man has a painful swelling on his shin.
It has slowly grown for years.
His tibia is bowed forward.
There is no history of injury.
X-ray shows multiple lytic lesions in the front of the tibia, like soap bubbles.
Biopsy shows epithelial cells in a fibrous stroma, positive for keratin.
A 45-year-old man has pain and swelling in his knee.
His knee locks at times.
He hears grinding when he moves it.
He has lost some movement.
X-ray shows many small calcified loose bodies of similar size in the joint.
Arthroscopy shows many cartilage nodules from the synovium.
A 30-year-old woman has a swollen knee.
It has been swollen on and off for a year.
She has had no injury.
Fluid drained from the knee is dark brown and bloody.
MRI shows a thick synovium with dark 'blooming' areas from hemosiderin.
Biopsy shows giant cells and hemosiderin-laden macrophages.
A 15-year-old girl dancer has pain in the ball of her foot.
It is worse when she stands on her toes.
She wears high heels often.
The second toe joint is swollen and tender.
Movement of the second toe is limited.
X-ray shows flattening and sclerosis of the second metatarsal head.
A 13-year-old girl has a bump on the back of her wrist.
Her wrist aches after sports.
She cannot fully turn her palm up.
She is short and her forearms and lower legs look short.
X-ray shows a bowed radius tilted toward the palm, with the ulna sticking out at the back.
Genetic testing shows a SHOX gene change (Leri-Weill dyschondrosteosis).
A 10-year-old boy has a very short neck.
His hairline at the back is low.
He cannot turn or bend his head much.
One shoulder blade sits high (Sprengel deformity).
Ultrasound shows he has only one kidney.
X-ray shows several fused cervical vertebrae.
A 22-year-old soldier has cramping calf pain when he runs.
It goes away quickly when he stops.
He does not smoke and has no risk factors.
His foot pulses are normal at rest.
The foot pulses vanish when he points his foot down against resistance.
MRI shows the popliteal artery running abnormally around the medial head of the gastrocnemius.
A 19-year-old ballet dancer has pain at the back of her ankle.
It hurts when she stands on pointe.
There is tenderness behind the ankle, in front of the Achilles tendon.
Forcing the foot down (plantarflexion) reproduces the pain.
X-ray shows a small separate bone behind the talus.
MRI shows bone edema and fluid around it.
A 25-year-old volleyball player has a dull ache at the back of his shoulder.
It is worse when he serves overhead.
He has numbness over the outer shoulder.
His deltoid looks smaller.
Pressing on the back of the shoulder is tender.
MRI shows atrophy of the teres minor.
A 30-year-old woman has tingling in her ring and little fingers.
It is worse when she raises her arms.
Her hand muscles are wasting.
Her pulse weakens when she turns her head.
X-ray shows a cervical rib.
Nerve studies show lower trunk damage.
A 3-year-old boy has been admitted for the sixth time with 'seizures'.
No one but his mother has ever seen one.
His mother is a former nurse and is very involved with the ward staff.
She asks for more tests and seems calm at bad news.
His blood sugar was very low last night, with a high insulin and a low C-peptide.
When he is cared for without his mother, all symptoms stop.
A 30-year-old man is in prison awaiting trial.
He suddenly seems confused.
Asked how many legs a dog has, he says 'five'.
Asked what colour snow is, he says 'green'.
He also says he hears voices and cannot recall recent events.
His brain scan and EEG are normal.
A 70-year-old woman says neighbours are poisoning her water.
Her sister, who lives with her, believes the same thing.
The two have lived alone together for decades and rarely see anyone else.
The older sister has had schizophrenia for years.
The younger sister has no past psychiatric history.
When they are separated, the younger sister's belief fades.
A 65-year-old woman has stopped eating.
She has been very depressed for months.
She says there is no point eating because her insides are rotten.
She says she has no blood.
She insists that she is already dead.
She has no signs of a stroke or dementia.
A 70-year-old man with Lewy body dementia is very upset.
He says the woman at home is not his wife.
He says she looks exactly like his wife.
He believes she is an impostor.
He recognises his wife's voice on the phone.
He has no problem recognising faces in general.
A 35-year-old woman says she is being followed everywhere.
She says the same man keeps changing his look to stay close to her.
She says the postman, a nurse and a bus driver are all really him in disguise.
She knows they look different but is sure they are one person.
She had a head injury a year ago.
She has no trouble recognising familiar faces.
A 60-year-old woman brings a small box to clinic.
It holds bits of skin, fluff and scabs.
She says they are bugs living under her skin.
She has scratched and picked her arms raw.
Skin scrapings and a skin biopsy show no mites or lice.
She remains certain she is infested.
A 16-year-old boy sleeps up to 20 hours a day.
This comes in episodes lasting one to two weeks, a few times a year.
When awake he eats huge amounts.
He is irritable, childish and sexually disinhibited, and says things feel unreal.
Between episodes he is completely normal.
His MRI, EEG and sleep studies between episodes are normal.
A 40-year-old man with chronic schizophrenia has a seizure on the ward.
Staff say he drinks water all day long.
He drinks from taps, showers and even toilets.
His sodium is 118 and his urine is very dilute.
His weight goes up during the day and down overnight.
In a water-deprivation test his urine concentrates normally.
A 60-year-old woman has taken haloperidol for 15 years.
She keeps chewing even when not eating.
Her tongue keeps darting out.
She grimaces and puckers her lips.
Her fingers make piano-playing movements.
The movements got worse when her dose was reduced.
A 35-year-old woman feels dizzy and sick.
She says she gets 'electric shocks' in her head when she moves her eyes.
She is irritable, tearful and sleeping badly with vivid dreams.
She has flu-like aches.
Three days ago she stopped her paroxetine suddenly.
The symptoms go away within a day of restarting it.
A 25-year-old man rushes to the emergency room in panic.
He says his penis is shrinking into his body.
He believes he will die when it fully retracts.
He is holding onto it tightly.
Several men in his village have had the same fear this week.
Examination is completely normal.
A 35-year-old man asks a surgeon to remove his healthy left leg above the knee.
He says since childhood the leg has felt like it does not belong to him.
He sometimes binds the leg up and uses crutches in private.
He knows the leg is healthy.
He is not psychotic and has no body image problem with anything else.
Neurological exam and brain scan are normal.
A 30-year-old nurse is admitted with recurrent skin abscesses.
Cultures grow mixed bowel bacteria.
She has scars from many past operations and has been to many hospitals.
She knows a lot of medical terms.
Staff find syringes in her locker.
She gains no money or leave from being ill.
A 60-year-old man accuses his wife of having an affair.
He checks her phone and underwear every day.
He has no real evidence.
He follows her to the shops.
He drinks heavily every night.
He has threatened to hurt her if she does not confess.
A 30-year-old man has a dry cough and breathlessness.
He smokes 30 cigarettes a day.
He suddenly had sharp chest pain last month from a collapsed lung.
He passes a lot of urine and is always thirsty.
CT shows nodules and odd-shaped cysts in the upper and middle zones, sparing the bases.
Lung biopsy shows cells positive for CD1a and langerin (CD207).
A 50-year-old man with liver cirrhosis is short of breath.
His breathing is worse when he sits or stands than when he lies flat.
His oxygen saturation also drops when he sits up.
He has clubbing and spider angiomas.
His chest X-ray and lung function tests are near normal.
Bubble echo shows bubbles in the left heart after three to six beats.
A 25-year-old woman had a stroke with no clear cause.
She has had many nosebleeds since childhood.
Her mother also has frequent nosebleeds.
There are small red spots on her lips and fingertips.
Her oxygen is low and she has clubbing.
CT shows a round lesion in the lung with a feeding artery and draining vein.
A 40-year-old man is more and more breathless.
He had chemotherapy with mitomycin years ago.
He has signs of right heart failure.
His DLCO is very low.
CT shows ground glass centrilobular nodules, septal lines and big lymph nodes.
He develops pulmonary edema when started on a pulmonary vasodilator.
A 20-year-old man had a bad chest infection as a baby.
He has had repeated chest infections.
He gets breathless on effort.
Chest X-ray shows one lung looks darker (hyperlucent).
On breathing out, the dark lung stays big (air trapping).
CT shows small pulmonary vessels and bronchiectasis in that lung.
A 15-year-old girl has had pneumonia in the same place three times.
It is always at the left lower lobe.
She coughs up a lot of sputum.
She is otherwise well.
CT shows a mass in the left lower lobe.
CT angiography shows it is supplied by an artery from the aorta.
A 30-year-old woman with lupus is suddenly short of breath.
She coughs up small streaks of blood.
Her hemoglobin has dropped by 3 g/dL in a day with no other bleeding.
Chest X-ray shows patchy shadows in both lungs.
Her DLCO is raised.
Bronchoalveolar lavage gets bloodier with each sample.
A 60-year-old man has a loud barking cough.
He has trouble clearing mucus and gets repeated chest infections.
He wheezes, but inhalers do not help.
He gets breathless when he coughs or laughs.
Spirometry shows a flattened flow loop when breathing out.
Dynamic CT and bronchoscopy show the trachea collapsing by more than half when he breathes out.
A 70-year-old slim woman has had a cough for a year.
She says she tends to hold back her coughing in public.
She is tall and thin with a curved spine and a flat chest.
She has tiredness and some weight loss.
CT shows bronchiectasis and tree-in-bud nodules in the right middle lobe and lingula.
Sputum grows Mycobacterium avium complex on repeated samples.
A 50-year-old man has got more breathless over two years.
Years ago he had a stem cell transplant.
He has lost a lot of weight and is very thin.
His chest looks flattened from front to back.
He has had a pneumothorax.
CT shows thick pleura and fibrosis at the top of both lungs, and biopsy shows elastic fibers.
A 45-year-old woman has a routine chest X-ray.
It shows several round nodules.
She has no cough or weight loss.
She had TB as a child.
CT shows several slowly growing nodules in both lungs; cancer is suspected.
Biopsy shows whorls of hyaline collagen, not cancer.
A 65-year-old man has had dull central abdominal pain on and off for months.
He sometimes has low fevers and feels full quickly.
He has lost a little weight.
Examination may show a vague central mass.
CT shows a hazy 'misty' mesentery around the vessels, with a fat ring sign.
Biopsy shows fat necrosis, chronic inflammation and fibrosis.
A 22-year-old swimmer has a swollen right arm.
It started after a week of hard training.
The arm feels heavy and aches.
The arm is blue and the veins over his chest wall are visible.
Doppler shows a clot in the subclavian vein.
Venography shows the vein squeezed between the first rib and the clavicle when he raises his arm.
A 6-year-old boy has a painful lump in his right groin.
He has had a known groin hernia for a year.
Now it is red, tender and cannot be pushed back.
He has a fever and has vomited.
His white count is high.
At surgery, the hernia sac contains an inflamed appendix.
A 40-year-old man has a tender lump in his groin.
He has had a small groin bulge for years.
Now it is painful and will not go back in.
He is still passing wind and stool, without vomiting.
CT shows a small blind-ending loop of bowel in the hernia.
At surgery, the hernia contains an inflamed Meckel diverticulum.
A 55-year-old woman has pain in her lower abdomen.
The pain is to one side of the midline.
It is worse when she strains or lifts.
She has a tender spot at the edge of her rectus muscle.
No lump can be felt, but there is tenderness when she tenses her abdomen.
CT shows a hernia through the aponeurosis lateral to the rectus, under the external oblique.
An 85-year-old very thin woman has vomiting and a swollen abdomen.
She has had crampy abdominal pain.
She has pain along the inside of her thigh down to the knee.
The pain gets worse when her hip is extended and turned inward.
There is no lump in her groin.
CT shows bowel trapped between the pectineus and obturator muscles.
An 80-year-old woman has vomiting and upper abdominal pain.
She has had gallstones for years.
She cannot keep anything down.
Her stomach is very swollen.
CT shows air in the bile ducts.
CT also shows a large gallstone blocking the duodenum.
A 30-year-old woman has a firm lump in her abdominal wall.
She had a baby by cesarean a year ago.
The lump is slowly growing.
It is fixed and painless.
Her father had familial adenomatous polyposis.
Biopsy shows bland spindle cells with nuclear beta-catenin.
